correctness.rationale: Joint Gaussian conditioning gives a conditional mean affine in the conditioning total and a conditional covariance independent of that total. A single residual Gaussian therefore couples all conditional laws. Nonnegative regression coefficients give an almost-sure coordinatewise coupling, hence multivariate stochastic order. Conversely, vector stochastic order implies stochastic order of every coordinate and therefore nondecreasing conditional means, forcing all regression coefficients to be nonnegative. For each coordinate, equal conditional variance makes likelihood-ratio ordering equivalent to the same mean-slope sign.

originality.rationale: The direct source explicitly identifies extension of its bivariate vector monotonicity result to the multivariate case as future research. Its multivariate Gaussian result is coordinatewise and only sufficient, using nonnegative covariance with the sum of the other variables. The new statement gives an if-and-only-if criterion for the full conditional Gaussian vector and simultaneously sharpens the coordinate likelihood-ratio condition. Candidate-specific semantic searches over Gaussian conditioning, row sums, Efron monotonicity, and multivariate stochastic order found no covering published record. The principal residual risk is implicit coverage by general equal-covariance Gaussian stochastic-order theory.
residual_risks: The theorem is an elementary consequence of Gaussian regression plus equal-covariance normal ordering, so older multivariate stochastic-order literature may contain an equivalent abstract statement without the Efron or conditional-sum terminology.
The finding resolves only the Gaussian subcase of the motivating multivariate extension direction, not arbitrary dependent distributions.
